excerpt: SignalWire, from the creators of FreeSWITCH, sells programmable voice, messaging, video and AI voice agents. Published per-minute pricing, funding and alternatives.
content:
SignalWire is a communications platform for developers: an API company in the same category as Twilio and Vonage. Developers use it to build phone and SMS features, video calls, contact centres and, increasingly, AI voice agents that answer and make calls. Its site calls it the communications control plane, with voice, messaging, video and AI on one programmable platform.

The company was founded by the creators and main maintainers of FreeSWITCH, a widely used open-source telephony engine, and Anthony Minessale is its cofounder and chief executive. It announced an $11.5 million Series A in August 2019 led by Storm Ventures, with Samsung NEXT and Sequoia Scouts. In June 2021 it announced a $30 million Series B led by Prosperity7 Ventures, taking its total funding to $41.6 million; T-Mobile Ventures and Deutsche Telekom later joined the round as strategic investors.

SignalWire publishes pay-as-you-go prices. Its AI Agent runtime costs $0.16 a minute, with voice transport billed on top, and the company says most customers pay roughly $0.163 to $0.168 a minute all-in for standard calls. US voice is $0.0066 a minute inbound and $0.008 outbound for local numbers, and $0.003 a minute for SIP or WebRTC. US SMS on local (10DLC) numbers is $0.00415 per segment, WhatsApp messages are $0.005 each, and a local phone number is $0.50 a month. Video conferencing is $0.0045 per participant-minute at 720p.

SignalWire suits developers and telecom teams building voice products, especially those who know FreeSWITCH or want AI voice agents with low latency. Teams that want a no-code phone system should look at a business phone service instead.

This profile is put together from the company's own pages and published reporting, checked on 15 October 2026. We have not tested the product, and nothing here is paid placement.
